raceSummary.headline: Still no major declarations, but post-midterm polls have scrambled both fields: Rubio leads Vance in two new surveys, and Ossoff is now second in the Democratic average.
paragraphs: Democrats won both chambers of Congress on Nov. 3, with at least 54 Senate seats and 254 House seats. Republicans are arguing over the cause, with JD Vance blaming the Iran war and Marco Rubio defending it.

An Emerson College poll taken Nov. 14–16 had Rubio ahead of Vance 44% to 24% among Republican voters, and a Verasight poll had Rubio ahead 33% to 27%; Echelon Insights still had Vance ahead 40% to 26%. Vance says he will "figure it out sometime next year." CNN reported on Nov. 19 that Rubio is weighing a run more seriously and has stopped repeating his pledge to back Vance. Reuters reported that Ted Cruz has begun early preparations and Glenn Youngkin is considering a bid. Gregory Bovino has had an exploratory committee since June.

On the Democratic side Kamala Harris leads the RealClearPolling average by only 1.5 points (16.5%) over Jon Ossoff (15%), who says he has no interest in running but led the Emerson poll. Buttigieg and Ocasio-Cortez are tied at 14%, and Newsom, who will decide in early January, has 11.3%. Buttigieg's advisers expect him to say yes within weeks or months, and Cory Booker is giving a run "a lot of hard thought."
